root_cause.text: In KVM/arm64, the fault injection and AT emulation paths (__kvm_find_s1_desc_level() and __kvm_at_s12()) performed page table walks via walk_s1() and kvm_walk_nested_s2() without holding kvm->srcu, leaving those walks unprotected against concurrent memslot changes.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly says “walk_s1() and kvm_walk_nested_s2() expect to be called while holding kvm->srcu to guard against memslot changes,” but “__kvm_at_s12() and __kvm_find_s1_desc_level() call into the respective walkers without taking kvm->srcu,” and the patch fixes this by wrapping both calls in scoped_guard(srcu, &vcpu->kvm->srcu).

intent_record.intent_summary: Protect the nested stage-2 walk with the KVM SRCU lock to prevent races while accessing KVM state.
intent_record.what: The direct call to kvm_walk_nested_s2(vcpu, ipa, &out) was wrapped inside a scoped_guard(srcu, &vcpu->kvm->srcu) block, adding SRCU protection around that function invocation while leaving the surrounding logic unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the nested stage-2 page table walk now executes while holding the KVM SRCU read-side lock, preventing concurrent teardown or modification of protected KVM structures during the walk and avoiding unsafe access or race conditions.

intent_record.intent_summary: Protect the guest stage-1 page-table walk with the KVM SRCU guard to fix missing synchronization during descriptor lookup.
intent_record.what: The direct call to walk_s1(vcpu, &wi, &wr, va) was wrapped in a scoped_guard(srcu, &vcpu->kvm->srcu) block, adding SRCU guard acquisition and automatic release around that page-table walk.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the stage-1 page-table walk now executes while holding the KVM SRCU read-side protection, preventing concurrent teardown or unsafe modification of KVM data structures during the walk and making the access synchronization correct.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly adds KVM SRCU protection around the nested stage-2 page table walk, matching the root cause of unprotected walks during AT/fault handling that could race with memslot updates.

The change directly adds KVM SRCU protection around the guest stage-1 page-table walk during descriptor lookup, matching the root cause of unprotected page-table walks in __kvm_find_s1_desc_level()/related paths against concurrent memslot changes.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the full implementation of the newly added AT S12 path, including the stage-2 walk call. In `__kvm_at_s12()`, after computing `ipa`, the code directly performs `ret = kvm_walk_nested_s2(vcpu, ipa, &out);` and there is no surrounding SRCU protection such as `srcu_read_lock(&vcpu->kvm->srcu)` / `srcu_read_unlock(...)`. The root cause states that AT emulation was vulnerable because `__kvm_at_s12()` performed page table walks via `kvm_walk_nested_s2()` without holding `kvm->srcu`, leaving the walk unprotected against concurrent memslot changes. That exact condition is present here. Since no SRCU acquisition/release or equivalent protection exists in this function, the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not yet included.

commit b8e625167a321138f83b1f6c99cf25d1290cb04e
Author: Marc Zyngier <maz@kernel.org>
Date:   Mon Aug 25 11:31:33 2025 +0100

    KVM: arm64: Add S1 IPA to page table level walker
    
    Use the filtering hook infrastructure to implement a new walker
    that, for a given VA and an IPA, returns the level of the first
    occurence of this IPA in the walk from that VA.
    
    This will be used to improve our SEA syndrome reporting.
    
    Reviewed-by: Oliver Upton <oliver.upton@linux.dev>
bic_trace_step.reason: The added function `__kvm_find_s1_desc_level()` directly performs a stage-1 page table walk by calling `walk_s1(vcpu, &wi, &wr, va);` under the comment `/* Walk the guest's PT, looking for a match along the way */`. The stated root cause is that fault injection / AT emulation paths performed walks via `walk_s1()` without holding `kvm->srcu`, leaving them unprotected against concurrent memslot changes. In this function body, there is no acquisition of `kvm->srcu` (no `srcu_read_lock`, no matching unlock, and no wrapper indicating the walk is protected). The function only calls `setup_s1_walk()` and then `walk_s1()` directly. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present. The fix is not present because the code still issues the page-table walk without any visible `kvm->srcu` protection.
